chunks: From him, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Ḥumrān, who said:

The sacrificial camels became scarce one year at Minā until a single camel reached one hundred dinars. So Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام was asked about that, and he said: “Share in it together.” He said: I said, “How many?” He said: “The fewer it is, the better.” He said: I said, “On behalf of how many does it suffice?” He said: “On behalf of seventy.”

key_terms.اشْتَرِكُوا: share jointly in the sacrificial animal
key_terms.الْبُدْنُ: the sacrificial camels offered in hajj
key_terms.بِمِنًى: at Minā, the hajj site where sacrifice is performed
key_terms.تُجْزِي: is sufficient and valid on behalf of
key_terms.دِينَارٍ: a gold coin used here as a measure of price

ai.seo_question: How many people can share in one sacrificial camel at Minā according to Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the sacrificial camel at Minā when prices become very high and obtaining one becomes difficult. Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام permits multiple people to share in one camel, while indicating that fewer participants are preferable, and that it may suffice for up to seventy people.
